title: Megabits Down to Kilobits: Memory-Efficient Time-Aware Shaping for TSN
problem: Memory-efficient Time-Aware Shaper (TAS) for Time-Sensitive Networking (TSN) in cyber-physical systems; traditional TAS stores per-frame gate control rules requiring tens of megabits of memory, exceeding switch capacity.
motivation: TSN provides bounded latency and low jitter for industrial control and cyber-physical systems; TAS gate control tables consume prohibitive memory (>10 Mbits) when supporting many flows, limiting deployment scalability.
method: Instead of storing control rules for every single frame, METAS keeps just one persistent rule per flow and generates specific frame-level rules on-demand. This approach trades memory for computation: less upfront storage but slightly more work when each frame arrives. An FPGA implementation demonstrates the payoff: memory usage drops from 14.34 megabits to 288 kilobits for 1,024 flows (a 98% reduction), using only 1.56% of FPGA logic resources while maintaining microsecond-level latency and nanosecond-level jitter guarantees.
key_novelty: Store a single rule per traffic flow and generate per-frame rules on-demand instead of storing them all, slashing memory by 98% while maintaining strict timing guarantees.
contributions: METAS per-flow approach with dynamic temporary rule generation
Memory reduction from 14.34 Mbits to 288 Kbits for 1,024 flows (98% reduction)
Microsecond-level latency and nanosecond-level jitter preservation
FPGA prototype using only 1.56% logic resources
